title: Treat tree-sitter offsets as UTF-16 code-unit indices, not UTF-8 bytes
context: sourceMutation.ts's spliceBytes() silently corrupted output when source files contained non-ASCII characters before mutation targets. Root cause: tree-sitter's startIndex/endIndex are UTF-16 code-unit offsets (matching JS char indices), not true UTF-8 byte offsets—but the code converted to Buffer and sliced as if they were bytes, causing misalignment for multi-byte UTF-8 sequences.
decision: Renamed spliceBytes → spliceChars and reimplemented using plain string slicing. Changed all index operations (including open-brace search for call injection) to work directly on the source string using character indices, eliminating UTF-8 byte conversion entirely. Added explicit documentation of the offset semantics.
consequences: Output is now correct for any non-ASCII source file, with exact target-span deletion even when preceding content is multi-byte
Implementation is simpler and faster (no Buffer allocation/conversion)
Contracts now explicitly document that offsets are character indices, not bytes, reducing future confusion
All existing callers continue to work without change
alternatives_rejected: Attempt to 'fix' UTF-8 byte handling in spliceBytes (would remain semantically wrong and fragile)
Seek true byte offsets from tree-sitter (tree-sitter does not provide them; the API returns char indices)
Add a UTF-8 byte ↔ char index converter (overcomplicated; offsets are already chars)
